title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck is building an axiomatic 'analysis situs' (tame topology) on a set \mathcal F of 'figures' with two basic relations: G \le F (G is a sous-figure, i.e. subfigure, of F) and G \preccurlyeq F (G is a subdivision of F). Earlier axioms C1-C7 are in force. From the previous page: C6 says a subfigure of a subdivision is a subdivision of a subfigure (G \le F' \preccurlyeq F implies there is G' with G \preccurlyeq G' \le F, the induced subdivision). C7_o says a subdivision of a subfigure extends to a subdivision of the whole (G' \preccurlyeq G \le F implies there is F' \preccurlyeq F with G' \le F'). C5 is used on the next page; it seems to concern disjointness under subdivision.

Definition. G refines F, written G \ll F, if there is F' with G \le F' \preccurlyeq F, i.e. G is a subfigure of a subdivision of F. By C6 and C7_o this is equivalent to G being a subdivision of a subfigure of F. In PL language, if figures are triangulated polyhedra, G \ll F is meant to say |G| \subseteq |F|. The order \ll is meant to recover the inclusion of underlying 'spaces' from the combinatorial data.

Corollary. \ll is an order relation, implied by both \le and \preccurlyeq.
- Reflexivity, and implication by \le and by \preccurlyeq: take F' = F, or G \le G.
- Transitivity. Suppose F \ll G \ll H, i.e. F \le G' \preccurlyeq G and G \le H' \preccurlyeq H.
  1. C6 applied to G \le H' \preccurlyeq H gives \bar H with G \preccurlyeq \bar H \le H.
  2. C6 applied to F \le G' \preccurlyeq G gives \bar G with F \preccurlyeq \bar G \le G.
  3. C6 applied to \bar G \le G \preccurlyeq \bar H gives K with \bar G \preccurlyeq K \le \bar H.
  This is diagram (*). Transitivity of \preccurlyeq and of \le gives F \preccurlyeq K \le H. C7_o converts this back to the defining form, so F \ll H.
- Antisymmetry. Take H = F, so F \ll G and G \ll F. Then F \preccurlyeq K \le F, and a Lemma gives K = F. Since K \le \bar H \le F, antisymmetry of \le gives \bar H = F, hence G \preccurlyeq F. Symmetrically F \preccurlyeq G, and antisymmetry of \preccurlyeq gives F = G.

Lemma (remaining to prove). If F \preccurlyeq K \le F, then K = F: a figure cannot be a subdivision of one of its proper subfigures.

The next page reduces this Lemma to a separation property of \le: if K < F, there is a nonempty G disjoint from K but not from F. It also remarks that this is not formal from C1-C4, with a counterexample using closed subsets of an ordered set.

Purpose: to build from the combinatorial pair (subfigure, subdivision) the intrinsic order of 'sub-spaces'. This is the axiomatic counterpart of passing from triangulations to polyhedra in a tame-topology framework, in the spirit of the Esquisse's 'topologie modérée'.
errors: The sentence 'on gagne, car F \preccurlyeq K \le H' gives the relation in the form 'subdivision of a subfigure'. To conclude F \ll H as defined (subfigure of a subdivision), one must invoke C7_o. This is implicit; the corollary does cite C7.

The diagram proof uses C6 three times. A shorter route is to apply C7_o once to G' \preccurlyeq G \le H', giving F \le X \preccurlyeq H' \preccurlyeq H. Grothendieck's longer route is justified because \bar H and K are reused in the antisymmetry argument.

Antisymmetry is reduced to the Lemma, which is left unproved on this page (it is deferred to the next page via a separation corollary and C5). The proof also tacitly uses antisymmetry and transitivity of both \le and \preccurlyeq.
A struck-out attempt (\bar G = F via F \preccurlyeq \bar G \preccurlyeq K) was abandoned in favour of the cleaner symmetric argument; no error remains.

ideas.what: Defining a refinement order G \ll F as 'subfigure of a subdivision' (equivalently 'subdivision of a subfigure'), meant to model inclusion of underlying polyhedra.
ideas.modern_name: Subcomplex of a subdivision, i.e. inclusion of subpolyhedra in PL topology; composite of two commuting relations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PL topology (Whitehead, Zeeman, Rourke-Sanderson) for the concrete notion; the abstract axiomatic version is unattributed
ideas.where_published: Only the general tame-topology program is in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5-6; this axiomatics is not there

ideas.what: Proof that the composite of the subfigure and subdivision relations is a partial order, using exchange laws C6/C7_o (the two composites agree).
ideas.modern_name: Composition of relations satisfying a distributive or exchange law (analogous to calculus of fractions / factorization of relations)

ideas.what: Lemma: a figure is not a subdivision of a proper subfigure of itself; noted to be non-formal and to need a separation axiom.
ideas.modern_name: Invariance of support under subdivision / non-collapsing of a polyhedron onto a proper subpolyhedron by subdivision

missed.claim: An axiomatic system C1-C7 for a 'category of figures' with subfigure and subdivision relations, from which the ordered set of subspaces is reconstructed. This is an unpublished attempt at axiomatizing tame topology combinatorially, close in spirit to but distinct from o-minimality. The order-theoretic core on this page is routine, but the axiomatic framework as a whole has not been developed in the literature.
missed.quote: On dit que G raffine F ou est un raffinement de F si \exists F' avec G \le F' \preccurlyeq F. On écrit G \ll F
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with o-minimal structures, stratified spaces and combinatorial models of PL topology, as a concrete fragment of Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' program. The page itself only proves an elementary order-theoretic corollary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains a clean but elementary order-theoretic corollary inside an unpublished axiomatic tame-topology framework. The framework is of historical interest, but this page's content is routine.
